chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: What a critic should be, and the danger of Times reviews
summary: Critics should report what happened and review last; one reviewer can kill a play.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I was going to ask. Suppose you were in charge of a magazine or newspaper, what criteria would you

That's a hard thing to say, because to me, I don't go to Broadway plays like I used to. But critics are supposed to write what is seen, in the case of -- for instance, I remember John Wilson reviewed a concert of mine. If he goes to a Beatle concert, he tells you there were millions of people there, and these guys sung that song, they sung the -- he'll tell you that they did the same things they've been doing. But an honest review -- when they review jazz, they don't give an honest review of what was seen, sung.

Because they're prejudiced. And critics are newspaper reporter, is all they're supposed to be. They're supposed to tell you what happened at the moment, how many people were there, what the reaction of the people was, what his feeling is is to be last.
And I've seen critics kill a good play. Because nobody give them enough money or something. I feel that a critic should be the last person to hear a record that's new, the last person --
You mean, let the record be out for a while.
That's right. And if anything -- if the people want to publicize, let them ask the public what
they think. They should not be allowed into a theatre until a year later. Maybe that's too long, maybe six months.

That's why I say, if that were the case, if the play had word of mouth, let's say, or a record, that word of mouth if it was good word of mouth would get around and you'd have people buying the thing before they knew that they weren't supposed to like it.

That's right, and why should the Times carry that much power, with one man to walk in and destroy a play? There's a play a friend of mine did, named Dan Wolfe. The critics just destroyed him in one night. And most of them didn't come.
What was the name of that play Dan Wolfe did?
(Inaudible) critics out, and have some-one hire a commercial critic out front, to interview the audience that came out, that play might have been a hit.
